title.zh: 评估：数据划分、验证与指标

description.en: Why training accuracy lies, how holdout, stratification and cross-validation estimate performance on unseen data, and every metric of the confusion matrix, with micro, macro and weighted averages by hand.
description.zh: 为什么训练准确率会骗人，留出法、分层和交叉验证怎样估计模型在新数据上的表现，以及混淆矩阵上的各种指标，包括手算 micro、macro、加权平均。

name.en: Train, validation and test; holdout and stratification
name.zh: 训练/验证/测试；留出与分层
混淆矩阵、准确率与基线

name.en: Precision, recall, F-score and the threshold
name.zh: 精确率、召回率、F 值与阈值

description.zh: 把训练准确率当作模型的好坏

description.zh: 在测试集上调超参数（数据泄漏）

title.en: What we are after: performance on data we have not seen
title.zh: 目标：在没见过的数据上表现好

text.en: A model is useful only on **new** cases. So the one question evaluation answers is: how well will this model do on data it was not trained on? Everything in this lesson is a way to answer it honestly.
text.zh: 模型只有在**新**数据上才有用。评估只回答一个问题：这个模型在没训练过的数据上会表现多好？这一课的所有做法，都是为了诚实地回答它。

items.en: Fit the model on the **training data**; measure it on **data held back** (validation or test).
items.zh: 用**训练数据**拟合模型；用**留出的数据**（验证或测试）来衡量。

items.en: This rests on two assumptions: the held-back instances come from the **same distribution** as the training ones, and instances are drawn **independently**.
items.zh: 这样做靠两个假设：留出的数据与训练数据**同分布**，且样本**相互独立**。

items.en: The inductive learning hypothesis (Mitchell): a hypothesis that fits a large enough training sample well will also fit unseen cases well. It is a hope about the data, not a theorem; evaluation is how we check it.
items.zh: 归纳学习假设（Mitchell）：在足够大的训练样本上拟合得好的假设，在没见过的样本上也会拟合得好。这是对数据的期望，不是定理；评估就是用来检验它。

prompt.en: A 1-nearest-neighbour classifier has 100% accuracy on its own training data. What does that tell us about its accuracy on new data?
prompt.zh: 1-近邻分类器在自己的训练数据上准确率是 100%。这说明它在新数据上的准确率……

label.en: Nothing: every training point is its own nearest neighbour, so 100% is guaranteed, whatever the model is worth.
label.zh: 什么也说明不了：每个训练点的最近邻就是它自己，所以 100% 是必然的，和模型好坏无关。

label.en: It will also be close to 100%.
label.zh: 也会接近 100%。

feedback.en: Training accuracy of 100% is built in for 1-NN (the point finds itself, distance 0). It is a statement about memorising, not about generalising.
feedback.zh: 1-NN 的训练准确率天生就是 100%（点会找到自己，距离为 0）。这说明的是记忆，不是泛化。

label.en: It will be exactly 50% on new data.
label.zh: 在新数据上正好是 50%。

feedback.en: Nothing fixes it at 50%; new-data accuracy depends on the problem. The point is that the training number carries no information.
feedback.zh: 没有什么把它固定在 50%；新数据的准确率取决于问题。关键是训练上的数字不含信息。

explain.en: Measuring on the data a model was fitted on rewards memorisation. Evaluation needs data the model has not touched.
explain.zh: 在拟合过的数据上量模型，奖励的是记忆。评估需要模型没碰过的数据。

alt.en: The labelled data split into train, validation and test, each with its job.
alt.zh: 有标签数据划成训练、验证、测试三份，各有用途。

text.en: Many methods have **hyperparameters** that training does not learn: $k$ in k-NN, the depth of a decision tree, $C$ in an SVM. To choose them we have to compare models, and that comparison needs data too.
text.zh: 很多方法有训练学不到的**超参数**（hyperparameter）：k-NN 的 $k$、决策树的深度、SVM 的 $C$。要选它们就得比较模型，而比较也需要数据。

rows.zh: 拟合参数（树的划分、权重）
比较超参数、选出最好的

rows.en: estimate the final model on unseen data
rows.zh: 估计最终模型在新数据上的表现

text.en: Procedure: choose the hyperparameter on validation data; then **refit on train + validation** with the chosen value; then look at the test set once.
text.zh: 流程：在验证集上选超参数；然后用选好的值在**训练+验证**上重新拟合；最后只看一次测试集。

prompt.en: You try depths 1 to 20 for a decision tree and keep the depth with the best accuracy on the test set. You report that accuracy. What is wrong?
prompt.zh: 你试了深度 1 到 20，保留测试集准确率最高的深度，并报告这个准确率。错在哪？

label.en: Nothing: the test set is the right place to compare models.
label.zh: 没错：测试集正是比较模型的地方。

feedback.en: If the test set picks the winner, there is no unseen data left to judge the winner. The best of 20 tries is biased upwards.
feedback.zh: 测试集挑出了赢家，就没有没见过的数据来评判赢家了。20 次里最好的那个，数值偏高。

label.en: The test set helped choose the model, so its score is optimistic: data leakage. Use a validation set (or cross-validation) to choose.
label.zh: 测试集参与了选模型，所以分数偏乐观：数据泄漏。应当用验证集（或交叉验证）来选。

label.en: Depth 20 is too many trials; try fewer depths.
label.zh: 试 20 个深度太多了，应该少试几个。

feedback.en: Fewer trials shrink the bias but do not remove it. The fix is to keep the test set out of the choice.
feedback.zh: 试得少只是让偏差变小，并没消除。办法是让测试集完全不参与选择。

explain.en: Leakage means information from the test set reached training or model choice. Then no data is left to test honestly.
explain.zh: 泄漏就是测试集的信息进入了训练或选模型的环节。这样就没有可以诚实检验的数据了。

title.zh: 留出法与随机子采样

text.en: **Holdout**: assign each instance at random to train or test, no overlap. Build the model on the training part only, evaluate on the test part only. Typical splits (train–test): 50–50, 80–20, 90–10.
text.zh: **留出法**（holdout）：随机把每个实例分到训练或测试，互不重叠。只用训练部分建模，只用测试部分评估。常见比例（训练–测试）：50–50、80–20、90–10。

text.en: **Random subsampling** repeats holdout several times with different random splits and averages the scores, so one unlucky split matters less.
text.zh: **随机子采样**（random subsampling）把留出法用不同的随机划分重复几次再取平均，这样一次倒霉的划分影响小一些。

rows.en: Simple to work with and implement
The size of the split matters (below)
rows.zh: 划分大小会影响结果（见下）

rows.en: Sampling bias: a random split can give train and test different distributions
rows.zh: 抽样偏差：随机划分可能让训练、测试分布不同

rows.en: Inefficient: the test data is never used for training
rows.zh: 资源利用低：测试数据从不参与训练

text.en: The size of the split
text.zh: 划分的大小

items.en: **Many test, few training** instances: the learner lacks information, so the model is worse than it could be and the score underestimates what all the data would give.
items.zh: **测试多、训练少**：学习器信息不足，模型比本可以做到的差，分数低估了用全部数据时的表现。

items.en: **Many training, few test** instances: an accurate model, but the small test set may not be representative, so the estimate can be too high or too low.
items.zh: **训练多、测试少**：模型准确，但测试集太小可能没有代表性，估计可能偏高也可能偏低。

title.zh: 分层：保持类别比例

text.en: Random splitting does not promise that the test set has the class mix of the data. With imbalanced data that is a real problem. **Stratification** forces every partition to keep the original class distribution.
text.zh: 随机划分不保证测试集的类别比例和原数据一致。数据不平衡时这是个真问题。**分层**（stratification）让每个划分都保持原来的类别分布。

text.en: Example: 100 instances, 10 of them positive, a random test set of 20. A random test set holds on average 2 positives, with a standard deviation of 1.21; with probability 9.5% it holds **none**, and then precision and recall are undefined. A stratified split gives exactly 2 every time.
text.zh: 例子：100 个实例，其中 10 个正例，随机抽 20 个做测试集。随机测试集平均含 2 个正例，标准差 1.21；有 9.5% 的概率**一个正例都没有**，这时精确率、召回率都无从算起。分层划分每次都恰好是 2 个。

rows.en: Preserves the distribution: every stratum is represented in the right proportion
rows.zh: 保持分布：每个子群都按正确比例出现

rows.en: More complex to implement than simple random sampling
rows.zh: 比简单随机抽样实现更复杂

rows.en: Small but important subgroups are still represented
rows.zh: 小而重要的子群也能被代表到

rows.en: As with holdout, some data is only for training and some only for testing
rows.zh: 和留出法一样，一部分数据只训练、一部分只测试

text.en: Stratification combines with holdout and with cross-validation.
text.zh: 分层可以和留出法、交叉验证结合。

alt.en: Five folds: each fold is the test fold once; the five scores are averaged.
alt.zh: 五折：每一折轮流当一次测试折；五个分数取平均。

items.en: Split the data into $k$ folds (stratified if the classes are imbalanced).
items.zh: 把数据分成 $k$ 折（类别不平衡就分层）。

items.en: In round $i$, fold $i$ is the test data and the other $k-1$ folds are the training data. Score it: $E_i$.
items.zh: 第 $i$ 轮，第 $i$ 折当测试数据，其余 $k-1$ 折当训练数据，得到分数 $E_i$。

items.en: Report the average of the $k$ scores.
items.zh: 报告 $k$ 个分数的平均。

text.en: **Leave-one-out** (LOOCV) is the extreme $k = N$: each instance is the test set once, the model is trained on the other $N-1$.
text.zh: **留一法**（leave-one-out，LOOCV）是极端的 $k = N$：每个实例轮流当一次测试集，模型用其余 $N-1$ 个训练。

rows.en: Every instance is used for both training and testing; the estimate reflects a dataset that looks like the whole data
rows.zh: 每个实例既训练又测试；估计反映的是像整体数据一样的数据集

rows.en: Trains on nearly all the data each time; no randomness in the split
rows.zh: 每次几乎用全部数据训练；划分没有随机性

text.en: How big is k?
text.zh: k 取多大？

items.en: **Fewer folds**: more instances per partition, more variance in the performance estimate, less work.
items.zh: **折数少**：每折实例多，性能估计方差更大，计算少。

items.en: **More folds**: fewer instances per partition, less variance, slower.
items.zh: **折数多**：每折实例少，方差更小，更慢。

items.en: The usual choice is $k = 10$ (sometimes 5): it mimics a 90–10 holdout, but far more reliably, because every instance takes a turn in the test fold.
items.zh: 常用 $k = 10$（有时 5）：它像 90–10 的留出法，但可靠得多，因为每个实例都轮到当测试数据。

prompt.en: With 10-fold cross-validation on 1000 instances, how many models are trained, and on how many instances each?
prompt.zh: 对 1000 个实例做 10 折交叉验证：训练多少个模型、每个用多少实例？

label.en: 10 models, 100 instances each
label.zh: 10 个模型，每个 100 个实例

feedback.en: 100 is the size of the test fold. Each model trains on the other $k - 1$ folds: 900.
feedback.zh: 100 是测试折的大小。每个模型用其余 $k - 1$ 折训练：900。

label.en: 1 model, 900 instances
label.zh: 1 个模型，900 个实例

feedback.en: That is a single 90–10 holdout. Cross-validation retrains from scratch in every round.
feedback.zh: 那是一次 90–10 的留出。交叉验证每一轮都重新训练。

label.en: 10 models, 900 instances each
label.zh: 10 个模型，每个 900 个实例

explain.en: Each round trains on $(k-1)/k$ of the data and tests on $1/k$; the cost is $k$ fits.
explain.zh: 每一轮用 $(k-1)/k$ 的数据训练、$1/k$ 测试；代价是拟合 $k$ 次。

title.en: Cross-validation for tuning, and which to use
title.zh: 用交叉验证调参，以及怎么选方法

text.en: Instead of a third set, tune with cross-validation **inside the training data**: for each candidate hyperparameter, run $k$-fold on the training data, average the $k$ validation scores, and keep the best candidate. Refit on all the training data; use the test set once at the end.
text.zh: 可以不留第三份数据，而是在**训练数据内部**用交叉验证调参：对每个候选超参数，在训练数据上做 $k$ 折，把 $k$ 个验证分数取平均，留下最好的。再用全部训练数据重新拟合；测试集最后只用一次。

rows.en: Better when data is small: every instance is used
rows.zh: 数据少时更好：每个实例都被用到
拟合 $k$ 次：大模型代价高
只有一次划分：估计不稳定

rows.en: Validation folds inside the training data
rows.zh: 训练数据内部的验证折

rows.en: A quick check, a final test set

prompt.en: Which is the best reason to prefer 10-fold cross-validation to a single 80–20 holdout on a dataset of 150 instances?
prompt.zh: 数据只有 150 个实例，相比一次 80–20 留出，更倾向 10 折交叉验证，最好的理由是？

label.en: It is faster than holdout.
label.zh: 它比留出法更快。

feedback.en: It is $k$ times slower, not faster. Speed is the reason to prefer holdout.
feedback.zh: 它慢 $k$ 倍，不是更快。要快才该选留出法。

label.en: It removes the need for a test set.
label.zh: 它让测试集变得不需要。

feedback.en: Cross-validation estimates performance; if you also tune on those folds, the final number is still optimistic. Keep a test set or use nested cross-validation.
feedback.zh: 交叉验证估计表现；如果你同时用这些折调参，最终数字仍偏乐观。要留测试集，或用嵌套交叉验证。

label.en: A 30-instance test set is small and noisy; averaging ten different test folds makes the estimate more stable and uses all the data.
label.zh: 30 个实例的测试集又小又噪；平均十个不同的测试折更稳，也用上了全部数据。

explain.en: Small data is where cross-validation earns its cost.
explain.zh: 数据少时，交叉验证的代价才值得。

title.en: The confusion matrix, accuracy and error rate
title.zh: 混淆矩阵、准确率与错误率

text.en: **Accuracy** is the fraction of correct predictions; the **error rate** is $1 -$ accuracy. A good start, but it does not say *which* mistakes the model makes. For two classes (positive = the one we look for) we tabulate all four outcomes:
text.zh: **准确率**（accuracy）是预测正确的比例，**错误率**（error rate）是 $1 -$ 准确率。它是个好的起点，但没告诉我们模型犯的是*哪种*错。两类时（正类 = 我们要找的那一类），把四种结果列成表：

blocks.tex: A = \frac{TP + TN}{TP + TN + FP + FN}, \qquad E = 1 - A

text.en: Rows are the **actual** class, columns the **predicted** class (the lectures' convention; some books swap them, so read the labels).
text.zh: 行是**实际**类别，列是**预测**类别（课件的约定；有的书反过来，所以先看标签）。

text.en: Not all errors cost the same. Calling a person with a viral infection healthy is a **false negative**; calling an innocent person a criminal is a **false positive**. We need metrics that look at each kind separately.
text.zh: 并非所有错误代价相同。把感染病毒的人判为健康是**假反例**；把无辜的人判为罪犯是**假正例**。我们需要分别看两类错误的指标。

title.zh: 精确率与召回率

rows.en: Of the actual positives, how many did we find?
rows.zh: 实际为正的里面，找到了多少？

rows.en: Of those we called positive, how many really are?
rows.zh: 我们判为正的里面，真是正的有多少？

rows.en: Of the actual negatives, how many did we clear?
rows.zh: 实际为负的里面，排除了多少？

rows.en: few false positives (recall of the negative class)
rows.zh: 假正例很少（负类的召回率）

text.en: Recall is about the **row** of actual positives, precision about the **column** of predicted positives. Specificity is not in the lectures; it is the recall of the negative class and appears in medical settings.
text.zh: 召回率看的是实际为正那一**行**，精确率看的是预测为正那一**列**。特异度（specificity）课件里没有；它是负类的召回率，医学里常见。

text.en: The deck's four-instance example (Red positive, Blue negative): TP = 1, FN = 1, FP = 2, TN = 0. Accuracy = 0.25; precision = 1/(1+2) = 0.333; recall = 1/(1+1) = 0.50.

prompt.en: Which metric matters most for an email spam filter, where losing a real email is costly? (Spam is the positive class.)
prompt.zh: 垃圾邮件过滤器丢掉正常邮件代价很高，最该看哪个指标？（垃圾邮件为正类）

label.en: Recall of the spam class.
label.zh: 垃圾邮件类的召回率。

feedback.en: Recall counts missed spam (false negatives), only an annoyance here. The costly mistake is a false positive, which precision penalises.
feedback.zh: 召回率数的是漏掉的垃圾邮件（假反例），这里只是烦人。代价高的是假正例，由精确率惩罚。

label.en: Precision of the spam class: a false positive is a real email in the spam folder.
label.zh: 垃圾邮件类的精确率：假正例就是把正常邮件放进了垃圾箱。

label.en: Accuracy, because it counts every mistake.
label.zh: 准确率，因为它把每个错误都算上了。

feedback.en: Accuracy weighs both kinds of mistake equally. When their costs differ, look at the one that hurts.
feedback.zh: 准确率给两种错误一样的权重。代价不同时，要看让你疼的那一种。

explain.en: Choose the metric by the cost of the mistake you cannot afford.
explain.zh: 按你付不起的那种错误的代价来选指标。

title.en: The threshold moves precision and recall in opposite directions
title.zh: 阈值一动，精确率和召回率反向变化

text.en: Most classifiers produce a **score** and call an instance positive when the score reaches a threshold $t$. Raise $t$ and fewer instances are called positive: those left are the sure ones, so precision tends to rise, but we miss more positives, so recall falls. Lower $t$ and the reverse.
text.zh: 多数分类器先给出一个**分数**，分数达到阈值 $t$ 才判为正。把 $t$ 抬高，判为正的变少，留下的都是把握大的，所以精确率往往上升，但会漏掉更多正例，召回率下降。把 $t$ 放低则相反。

alt.en: Recall and precision against the threshold for six positive and ten negative instances.
alt.zh: 六个正例、十个负例时，召回率和精确率随阈值的变化。

text.en: Recall can only fall as $t$ rises (a positive called positive at a high threshold is also called positive at a lower one). Precision can wiggle: here it is 0.50 at $t = 0.3$ and at $t = 0.5$, but 0.60 at 0.7. So “inverse relationship” is a tendency, not a law.
text.zh: $t$ 升高时召回率只会下降（高阈值下被判为正的，在低阈值下也是正）。精确率可能起伏：这里 $t = 0.3$ 和 $t = 0.5$ 时都是 0.50，在 0.7 时是 0.60。所以“此消彼长”是倾向，不是定律。

text.en: If you care about only one of them, push the threshold that way. Usually we want both, so we combine them into one number.
text.zh: 如果只在乎其中一个，就把阈值往那个方向推。通常两个都要，所以把它们合成一个数。

title.zh: F 值：把两者合成一个数

say.en: The **F1-score** is the **harmonic mean** of precision $P$ and recall $R$. Why not the plain average? With $P = 1$ and $R = 0.01$ (call everything negative except one sure case) the average is 0.505, which looks fine; $F_1 = 0.0198$ tells the truth. The harmonic mean is dragged toward the smaller one.
say.zh: **F1 值**是精确率 $P$ 和召回率 $R$ 的**调和平均**。为什么不用普通平均？当 $P = 1$、$R = 0.01$（几乎全判为负、只挑一个最有把握的），平均是 0.505，看上去还行；$F_1 = 0.0198$ 才说出真相。调和平均被较小的那个拉下去。

say.en: Write $P$ and $R$ with their counts.
say.zh: 把 $P$ 和 $R$ 用计数写出来。

say.en: The numerator: multiply the two fractions.
say.zh: 分子：把两个分数相乘。

say.en: The denominator: put both fractions over the common denominator $(TP+FP)(TP+FN)$.
say.zh: 分母：通分到 $(TP+FP)(TP+FN)$。

say.en: Divide: the common denominator cancels, and so does one $TP$. This form is the fastest to compute from the matrix. Note that **TN never appears**.
say.zh: 相除：公共分母约掉，一个 $TP$ 也约掉。这个形式从矩阵里算最快。注意：**TN 根本没出现**。

say.en: Check on the four-instance example ($TP = 1$, $FP = 2$, $FN = 1$). The deck writes 0.398 because it rounded $P$ to 0.33 first; the exact value is 0.4. Round at the end, not in the middle.
say.zh: 用四实例的例子检验（$TP = 1$、$FP = 2$、$FN = 1$）。课件写 0.398 是因为先把 $P$ 舍成了 0.33；精确值是 0.4。要最后再舍入，不要中途舍入。

outro.en: **F-beta** generalises it: $F_\beta = \dfrac{(1+\beta^2)PR}{\beta^2 P + R}$. $\beta > 1$ favours recall, $\beta < 1$ favours precision, $\beta = 1$ is F1. At the threshold $t = 0.5$ above, $P = 0.50$, $R = 0.67$: $F_1 = 0.57$ and $F_2 = 0.62$ (recall is larger, so $F_2$ is higher).
outro.zh: **F-beta** 是它的推广：$F_\beta = \dfrac{(1+\beta^2)PR}{\beta^2 P + R}$。$\beta > 1$ 偏重召回率，$\beta < 1$ 偏重精确率，$\beta = 1$ 就是 F1。上面 $t = 0.5$ 时 $P = 0.50$、$R = 0.67$：$F_1 = 0.57$，$F_2 = 0.62$（召回率更大，所以 $F_2$ 更高）。

title.en: Why accuracy fails on imbalanced data
title.zh: 为什么类别不平衡时准确率会失效

say.en: Start from the definition; $N$ is the number of instances. Let $N_+ = TP + FN$ be the actual positives and $N_- = TN + FP$ the actual negatives.
say.zh: 从定义出发；$N$ 是实例总数。设 $N_+ = TP + FN$ 为实际正例数，$N_- = TN + FP$ 为实际负例数。

say.en: Split the numerator, then multiply and divide the first term by $N_+$ and the second by $N_-$. Nothing changed; we only introduced two ratios.
say.zh: 拆开分子；第一项乘除 $N_+$，第二项乘除 $N_-$。数值没变，只是引入了两个比值。

say.en: The ratios have names: $TP/N_+ = R$ is recall, $TN/N_- = S$ is specificity, $A$ is accuracy, and $\pi = N_+/N$ is the share of positives. **Accuracy is a weighted average of the recall on each class, weighted by class size.**
say.zh: 这些比值有名字：$TP/N_+ = R$ 是召回率，$TN/N_- = S$ 是特异度，$A$ 是准确率，$\pi = N_+/N$ 是正例所占比例。**准确率是各类召回率按类别大小加权的平均。**

say.en: The majority-class baseline (Zero-R) never says positive: $R = 0$, $S = 1$.
say.zh: 多数类基线（Zero-R）从不判为正：$R = 0$、$S = 1$。

say.en: The deck's disease example (1% sick). A model that detects **no** sick person scores 99%. Detecting every sick person raises accuracy by at most the weight of the positive class: 0.01.
say.zh: 课件里的疾病例子（1% 患病）。一个**一个病人都检测不出**的模型得 99%。把所有病人都检出来，准确率最多再涨正类的权重：0.01。

outro.en: So always compare accuracy with the **baseline**: Zero-R gives $1-\pi$; One-R is the best single-feature rule; random guessing with the class proportions gives $\pi^2 + (1-\pi)^2$. Accuracy 99% means little when the baseline is 99%; accuracy 60% can be excellent on a hard task whose baseline is 20%. Then look at per-class precision and recall.
outro.zh: 所以永远把准确率和**基线**（baseline）比较：Zero-R 是 $1-\pi$；One-R 是最好的单特征规则；按类别比例随机猜是 $\pi^2 + (1-\pi)^2$。基线是 99% 时，准确率 99% 毫无意义；基线是 20% 的难任务上，60% 可能已经很棒。然后再看各类的精确率和召回率。

prompt.en: Put $\pi = 0.01$, recall 0 and specificity 1 into the formula.
prompt.zh: 把 $\pi = 0.01$、召回率 0、特异度 1 代入公式。

title.en: More than two classes: one class against the rest
title.zh: 多于两类：一类对其余所有类

text.en: With classes Red, Blue, Gold there is no single “positive”. Pick one **interesting** class and treat all others as “negative”; read TP, FP, FN, TN from the matrix for that class; repeat for every class.
text.zh: 有红、蓝、金三类时就没有唯一的“正类”。选一个**关注的**类，把其余类都当作“负类”；从矩阵里读出这一类的 TP、FP、FN、TN；对每一类重复。

text.en: The deck's example (5 instances): actual Red, Blue, Red, Blue, Gold; predicted Red, Red, Blue, Red, Blue. Rows are actual, columns predicted:
text.zh: 课件的例子（5 个实例）：实际为红、蓝、红、蓝、金；预测为红、红、蓝、红、蓝。行是实际，列是预测：

items.en: **TP** of a class: its diagonal cell.
items.zh: 某类的 **TP**：它的对角线格子。

items.en: **FN**: the rest of its **row** (actually this class, predicted as another).
items.zh: **FN**：它所在**行**的其余格子（实际属于这类，被预测成别的）。

items.en: **FP**: the rest of its **column** (predicted as this class, actually another).
items.zh: **FP**：它所在**列**的其余格子（被预测成这类，实际是别的）。

body.en: Gold is never predicted, so its precision is $0/0$. The deck sets it to 0 (so does scikit-learn, with a warning). Say so in an answer instead of hiding it.
body.zh: 金从来没被预测过，所以它的精确率是 $0/0$。课件把它定为 0（scikit-learn 也如此，并给出警告）。答题时把这个约定写出来，不要藏着。

title.en: Macro, micro and weighted: the deck example by hand
title.zh: macro、micro、加权：课件例子手算

say.en: **Macro**: compute the metric per class, then take the plain average. Every class counts the same, whatever its size.
say.zh: **Macro**：先按类算指标，再取简单平均。每一类权重相同，不管大小。

say.en: Same for recall: Red $\tfrac12$, Blue 0, Gold 0.
say.zh: 召回率同样：红 $\tfrac12$，蓝 0，金 0。

say.en: **Micro**: pool all instances first. Add the counts over classes ($\sum TP = 1$, $\sum FP = 2 + 2 + 0 = 4$), then compute once. Every *instance* counts the same.
say.zh: **Micro**：先把所有实例汇总。把各类的计数相加（$\sum TP = 1$，$\sum FP = 2 + 2 + 0 = 4$），再算一次。每个*实例*权重相同。

say.en: Here $\sum FN = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4$. Micro precision and micro recall are equal, and equal to the accuracy, 0.2. (Proved in the next lesson step.)
say.zh: 这里 $\sum FN = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4$。micro 精确率和 micro 召回率相等，也等于准确率 0.2。（下一步证明。）

say.en: **Weighted**: per-class metric averaged with weights $n_c / N$, the class's share of the instances (Red 2, Blue 2, Gold 1 out of 5). The deck prints 0.132 because it used 0.33; exactly it is 2/15.
say.zh: **加权**：按类算指标，用 $n_c / N$（类 $c$ 的实例占比：红 2、蓝 2、金 1，共 5）加权平均。课件印的是 0.132，因为用了 0.33；精确值是 2/15。

say.en: Weighted recall is 0.2 too: it also equals the accuracy (shown in the next step).
say.zh: 加权召回率也是 0.2：它同样等于准确率（下一步证明）。

outro.en: **Summary** (precision / recall): macro 0.111 / 0.167; micro 0.20 / 0.20; weighted 0.133 / 0.20; accuracy 0.20. Macro F1 (the average of the per-class F1 values 0.4, 0, 0) is 0.133; micro F1 is 0.20.

prompt.en: Average the three per-class recalls: $\tfrac12$, 0, 0 (three decimals).
prompt.zh: 把三个类的召回率平均：$\tfrac12$、0、0（保留三位小数）。

title.en: A skewed example: when each average misleads
title.zh: 一个偏斜的例子：每种平均何时误导

text.en: The deck's second example has a big class (Red, 200 instances) and two small ones (Blue 20, Gold 10):
text.zh: 课件的第二个例子有一个大类（红，200 个实例）和两个小类（蓝 20，金 10）：

text.en: Accuracy is 0.81, and micro and weighted recall say the same. Yet the model finds only 25% of Blue and 10% of Gold. Macro recall, 0.42, shows it.
text.zh: 准确率是 0.81，micro 和加权召回率也这么说。但模型只找到了 25% 的蓝和 10% 的金。macro 召回率 0.42 才暴露了这一点。

items.en: **Micro** (and weighted recall) is dominated by the large class. Use it when each *instance* matters equally; it can hide a failing minority class.
items.zh: **Micro**（以及加权召回率）被大类主导。每个*实例*同等重要时用它；它会掩盖失败的少数类。

items.en: **Macro** treats classes equally and emphasises small ones. Use it when every *class* matters equally. It can mislead the other way: Gold's precision is 1.00 from a single prediction, yet it supplies a third of the macro precision.
items.zh: **Macro** 对各类一视同仁，强调小类。每个*类别*同等重要时用它。它也可能反向误导：金只预测了一次，精确率就是 1.00，却贡献了 macro 精确率的三分之一。

items.en: **Weighted** weights classes by size: close to micro, but keeps per-class precision and recall separate (its precision can differ from its recall).
items.zh: **加权**按类别大小加权：接近 micro，但保留了各类的精确率和召回率（它的精确率可以不等于召回率）。

prompt.en: A detector must be judged on how well it finds each of 12 rare diseases, whose frequencies differ a hundredfold. Which average?
prompt.zh: 一个检测器要按它找出 12 种罕见病各自的能力来评判，这些病的发病率相差上百倍。用哪种平均？

label.en: Micro: it uses all the instances.
label.zh: micro：它用到了所有实例。

feedback.en: Micro is dominated by the frequent diseases; a detector that misses every rare disease can still score high.
feedback.zh: micro 被常见病主导；漏掉所有罕见病的检测器照样可以得高分。

label.en: Weighted: the fairest compromise.
label.zh: 加权：最公平的折中。

feedback.en: Weighting by frequency again lets the common diseases dominate, just what we wanted to avoid.
feedback.zh: 按频率加权又让常见病占主导，这正是我们想避免的。

label.en: Macro: every disease counts the same, however rare.
label.zh: macro：每种病权重相同，不管多罕见。

explain.en: Choose the average by what should count equally: classes (macro) or instances (micro).
explain.zh: 按“什么该被同等看待”来选平均：类别（macro）还是实例（micro）。

title.en: Deeper: why micro-F1 equals accuracy for single-label problems
title.zh: 深入：为什么单标签多分类里 micro-F1 等于准确率

say.en: Summing the diagonal counts every correctly classified instance once; call that number $M$.
say.zh: 把对角线加起来，每个分类正确的实例恰好算一次；记这个数为 $M$。

lines.tex: y = a,\ \hat y = b,\ b \neq a

say.en: Each wrong instance has exactly one true class $a$ and one predicted class $b \ne a$ (single-label: one label each).
say.zh: 每个分类错误的实例恰有一个真类 $a$ 和一个预测类 $b \ne a$（单标签：各一个标签）。

say.en: It is missed by class $a$ (FN) and wrongly claimed by class $b$ (FP): the same mistake counted once on each side.
say.zh: 它被 $a$ 类漏掉（FN），又被 $b$ 类错认（FP）：同一个错误在两边各记一次。

say.en: So both sums equal the number of wrong instances.
say.zh: 所以两个和都等于错误实例的个数。

say.en: Check on the deck's 5-instance example: $\sum TP = 1$, $\sum FP = 4$, and together they make $N$. In general $\sum TP + \sum FP = \sum TP + (N - \sum TP) = N$.
say.zh: 用课件的 5 实例例子检验：$\sum TP = 1$，$\sum FP = 4$，加起来就是 $N$。一般地 $\sum TP + \sum FP = \sum TP + (N - \sum TP) = N$。

lines.tex: P_\mu = \frac{\sum TP}{\sum TP + \sum FP} = \frac{\sum TP}{N} = A

say.en: So the micro-precision denominator is $N$.
say.zh: 所以 micro 精确率的分母是 $N$。

lines.tex: R_\mu = \frac{\sum TP}{\sum TP + \sum FN} = \frac{\sum TP}{N} = A

say.en: Same for recall. Both equal the accuracy.
say.zh: 召回率同理。两者都等于准确率。

say.en: With $P = R = A$ the harmonic mean is just $A$. So reporting micro-F1 adds nothing beyond accuracy.
say.zh: $P = R = \text{Acc}$ 时调和平均就是 Acc。所以报告 micro-F1 不比准确率多给任何信息。

say.en: The same trick for weighted recall: the class sizes $n_c$ cancel.
say.zh: 加权召回率同理：类别大小 $n_c$ 约掉了。

outro.en: Take-away for the exam: in a single-label multiclass problem, micro precision = micro recall = micro F1 = accuracy. Only macro and weighted averages carry extra information.
outro.zh: 考试要点：单标签多分类里，micro 精确率 = micro 召回率 = micro F1 = 准确率。只有 macro 和加权平均才带来额外信息。

prompt.en: How many instances are there? ($\sum TP + \sum FP$ should come out as this number.)
prompt.zh: 一共有多少个实例？（$\sum TP + \sum FP$ 应该等于这个数。）

title.en: Regression metrics: the size of the error
title.zh: 回归指标：误差有多大

text.en: For a numeric target there is no right or wrong, only how far off. With error $y_i - \hat y_i$ on test instance $i$:
text.zh: 目标是数值时没有对错，只有差多远。第 $i$ 个测试实例的误差是 $y_i - \hat y_i$：

rows.en: sum of squared errors; what least squares minimises
rows.zh: 平方误差之和；最小二乘最小化的量

rows.en: penalises large errors more; sensitive to outliers
rows.zh: 更重地惩罚大误差；对离群点敏感

rows.en: same units as the target, so easier to read
every error counts in proportion; less sensitive to outliers
rows.zh: 每个误差按比例计入；对离群点不那么敏感

text.en: Example: actual $y = (3, 5, 2, 7, 4)$, predicted $\hat y = (2.5, 5.5, 2, 6, 7)$. Errors: $0.5, -0.5, 0, 1, -3$. SSE = 10.50, MSE = 2.10, RMSE = 1.449, MAE = 1.00. The one big miss (error 3) is 3 of the 5 absolute-error units but 86% of the squared error.
RMSE is always at least MAE; the bigger the gap, the more of the error comes from a few large misses (here 1.449 against 1.00).
text.zh: RMSE 永远不小于 MAE；差距越大，说明误差越集中在少数大失误上（这里 1.449 对 1.00）。

text.en: $SST$ is the squared error of the “baseline” that always predicts the mean $\bar y$ (the regression Zero-R). So $R^2 = 1$ is perfect, 0 is no better than the mean, and negative is worse. Here $SST = 14.80$, so $R^2 = 0.29$.
text.zh: $SST$ 是总是预测均值 $\bar y$ 的“基线”（回归里的 Zero-R）的平方误差。所以 $R^2 = 1$ 是完美，0 是不比均值好，负数是更糟。这里 $SST = 14.80$，所以 $R^2 = 0.29$。

title.en: Deeper: why MSE chases outliers and MAE does not
title.zh: 深入：为什么 MSE 追着离群点跑，而 MAE 不会

say.en: Suppose the model can only predict one constant $c$. Which $c$ minimises the squared error?
say.zh: 假设模型只能预测一个常数 $c$。哪个 $c$ 让平方误差最小？

say.en: Differentiate and set to zero.
say.zh: 求导并令其为零。

say.en: The squared-error optimum is the **mean**. One huge $y_i$ drags the mean, so the fit chases it.
say.zh: 平方误差的最优解是**均值**。一个巨大的 $y_i$ 会拽动均值，拟合就追着它走。

say.en: For absolute error each point pulls with a constant force $\pm 1$, however far away it is. Balance: as many points below $c$ as above.
say.zh: 绝对误差下，每个点以恒定的力 $\pm 1$ 拉，不论离多远。平衡点：$c$ 下方和上方的点一样多。

say.en: The absolute-error optimum is the **median** $\tilde y$, which a single outlier hardly moves.
say.zh: 绝对误差的最优解是**中位数** $\tilde y$，一个离群点几乎拽不动它。

outro.en: So the choice of metric is a choice of what to care about: MSE/RMSE if large misses are especially costly, MAE if you want robustness to outliers.
outro.zh: 所以选指标就是选在乎什么：大失误代价特别高，用 MSE/RMSE；想对离群点稳健，用 MAE。

title.zh: 由混淆矩阵算 F1

prompt.en: A classifier on 200 test instances gives $TP = 40$, $FP = 10$, $FN = 20$, $TN = 130$. What is the F1-score of the positive class? (Two decimals.)
prompt.zh: 分类器在 200 个测试实例上得到 $TP = 40$、$FP = 10$、$FN = 20$、$TN = 130$。正类的 F1 是多少？（两位小数。）

explain.en: $F_1 = \dfrac{2TP}{2TP + FP + FN} = \dfrac{80}{110} = 0.727$. Via the parts: precision $40/50 = 0.8$, recall $40/60 = 0.667$, harmonic mean 0.727. TN plays no role.

title.zh: macro 平均精确率

prompt.en:
Three classes, confusion matrix below (rows actual, columns predicted; order A, B, C):

A: 18, 1, 1
B: 3, 4, 3
C: 1, 0, 4

What is the macro-averaged precision? (Three decimals.)
prompt.zh:
三类的混淆矩阵如下（行为实际，列为预测；顺序 A、B、C）：

A: 18, 1, 1
B: 3, 4, 3
C: 1, 0, 4

macro 平均精确率是多少？（三位小数。）

explain.en: Precision is per **column**: A $18/22 = 0.818$, B $4/5 = 0.800$, C $4/8 = 0.500$. Macro = their plain average = 0.706. (Macro recall would be 0.700; micro = accuracy = 0.743.)

hints.en: Column sums are 22, 5, 8; the diagonal is 18, 4, 4.

title.zh: 找出泄漏

prompt.en: A student standardises the features with the mean and standard deviation of the **whole** dataset, then runs 10-fold cross-validation and reports 94% accuracy. What is the problem?
prompt.zh: 一位同学用**整个**数据集的均值和标准差对特征做标准化，然后做 10 折交叉验证，报告 94% 的准确率。问题是什么？

label.en: 10 folds is too few.
label.zh: 10 折太少了。

feedback.en: The number of folds is not the issue; the order of operations is.
feedback.zh: 问题不在折数，而在操作顺序。

label.en: Information from the test folds (their mean and spread) leaked into training; the estimate is optimistic. Compute the scaling on the training folds only.
label.zh: 测试折的信息（均值和离散程度）漏进了训练；估计偏乐观。应只用训练折来计算缩放参数。

label.en: Standardising should not be done in cross-validation at all.
label.zh: 交叉验证里根本不该做标准化。

feedback.en: Standardise, but **inside** each round, fitted on that round's training folds and applied to its test fold.
feedback.zh: 要做，但要在每一轮**内部**做：用该轮训练折拟合，再应用到它的测试折。

label.en: The folds should not be stratified.
label.zh: 折不该分层。

feedback.en: Stratification is harmless here and unrelated to the leak.
feedback.zh: 分层在这里无害，和泄漏无关。

explain.en: Anything learned from data (scaling, feature selection, hyperparameters) must be learned from the training part of each round only.
explain.zh: 任何从数据里学来的东西（缩放、特征选择、超参数）都只能从每一轮的训练部分学。

title.zh: 欺诈检测器

prompt.en: Only 0.5% of transactions are fraudulent. A model has 99.4% accuracy. Which conclusion is justified?
prompt.zh: 只有 0.5% 的交易是欺诈。某模型准确率 99.4%。下面哪个结论成立？

label.en: The model is excellent.
label.zh: 模型很出色。

feedback.en: 99.4% is below the 99.5% baseline of “never fraud”. It may be worse than doing nothing.
feedback.zh: 99.4% 低于“从不判欺诈”的基线 99.5%。它可能还不如什么都不做。

label.en: The model is poor because 99.4% is below 100%.
label.zh: 模型很差，因为 99.4% 低于 100%。

feedback.en: 100% is not the right yardstick; the baseline is. Poor or not depends on the fraud-class metrics.
feedback.zh: 100% 不是合适的尺子，基线才是。差不差要看欺诈类的指标。

label.en: Nothing yet: the Zero-R baseline already scores 99.5%, so this model is below it. Look at precision and recall on the fraud class.
label.zh: 还不能下结论：Zero-R 基线已经是 99.5%，这个模型还低于它。要看欺诈类的精确率和召回率。

label.en: Switch to micro-averaged F1 to fix it.
label.zh: 改用 micro 平均 F1 就能解决。

feedback.en: With single labels, micro-F1 equals accuracy: it would say 0.994 again.
feedback.zh: 单标签时，micro-F1 就等于准确率：它还是 0.994。

explain.en: Compare with the baseline and look at the minority class. Micro averages cannot rescue you: they are accuracy in disguise.
explain.zh: 和基线比较，并看少数类。micro 平均救不了你：它就是换了名字的准确率。

title.zh: 手算 RMSE

prompt.en: Actual values $(10, 20, 30)$, predictions $(12, 18, 36)$. What is the RMSE? (Two decimals.)

title.zh: 留出法与 k 折比较

prompt.en: Compare the holdout method and k-fold cross-validation as ways of estimating a classifier's performance. Give two points for each and say when you would use which. (3 to 5 lines)
prompt.zh: 比较留出法和 k 折交叉验证这两种估计分类器性能的方法。各给两点，并说明什么时候用哪个。（3 到 5 行）

key_points.en: Holdout: one random train/test split; simple, fast, reproducible
key_points.zh: 留出法：一次随机划分训练/测试；简单、快、可复现

key_points.en: Holdout weaknesses: result depends on the split and its size; test data is never used for training
key_points.zh: 留出法缺点：结果依赖划分及其大小；测试数据不参与训练

key_points.en: k-fold: every instance is tested once and used for training k-1 times; the k scores are averaged, so the estimate is more stable
key_points.zh: k 折：每个实例测试一次、训练 k-1 次；k 个分数取平均，估计更稳

key_points.en: k-fold costs k model fits (leave-one-out: N)
key_points.zh: k 折要拟合 k 次（留一法：N 次）

key_points.en: Use holdout for large data or expensive models; k-fold (stratified for imbalance) for small data and for comparing or tuning
key_points.zh: 数据大或模型贵用留出法；数据少、要比较或调参用 k 折（不平衡时分层）

model_answer.en: Holdout splits the data once at random into train and test (e.g. 80-20). It is simple, fast and reproducible, but the estimate depends on which instances land in the test set and on its size, and the test instances are never used for training. k-fold cross-validation splits the data into k folds; each fold is the test set once while the others train, and the k scores are averaged. Every instance is used for both training and testing and the estimate is more stable, but it needs k model fits. I would use holdout when data is plentiful or training is expensive, and (stratified) k-fold, typically k = 10, when data is small or I need a reliable comparison or hyperparameter tuning.
model_answer.zh: Holdout splits the data once at random into train and test (e.g. 80-20). It is simple, fast and reproducible, but the estimate depends on which instances land in the test set and on its size, and the test instances are never used for training. k-fold cross-validation splits the data into k folds; each fold is the test set once while the others train, and the k scores are averaged. Every instance is used for both training and testing and the estimate is more stable, but it needs k model fits. I would use holdout when data is plentiful or training is expensive, and (stratified) k-fold, typically k = 10, when data is small or I need a reliable comparison or hyperparameter tuning.

explain.en: The exam wants contrasts with a reason, not a list of names.
explain.zh: 考试要的是带理由的对比，不是名词罗列。

title.zh: 设计一个评估（C 部分风格）

prompt.en: A hospital wants a classifier that flags a rare disease (2% of patients) from scan features. The dataset has 500 patients and several scans per patient. Describe how you would evaluate it: how to split, which metrics, and what to compare against. (A third of a page)
prompt.zh: 医院想用扫描特征训练一个分类器来标出某种罕见病（2% 的患者）。数据有 500 名患者，每人有多次扫描。请说明你会怎样评估：怎么划分、用哪些指标、和什么比较。（约三分之一页）

key_points.en: Split by patient, not by scan, so no patient is in both train and test
key_points.zh: 按患者而不是按扫描划分，同一患者不同时出现在训练和测试里

key_points.en: Stratify on the disease label (cross-validation or holdout) to keep the 2% in every part
key_points.zh: 按疾病标签分层（交叉验证或留出），让每份都保持 2%

key_points.en: Metrics: recall (missed cases), precision, F1 on the disease class; not accuracy alone
key_points.zh: 指标：疾病类的召回率（漏诊）、精确率、F1；不能只看准确率

key_points.en: Baseline: Zero-R scores 98% accuracy; the model must beat it on recall/F1
key_points.zh: 基线：Zero-R 准确率 98%；模型要在召回率/F1 上胜过它

key_points.en: Tune hyperparameters on validation folds only; touch the test set once
key_points.zh: 超参数只在验证折上调；测试集只碰一次

model_answer.en: I would split by patient so that scans of one patient never appear in both training and test data (otherwise the model can recognise the patient and the estimate is optimistic). With 500 patients and about 10 positives, I would use stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 5), keeping the 2% positive rate in each fold, tuning hyperparameters inside the training folds and keeping a final test set untouched until the end. I would not use accuracy, since the Zero-R baseline already has 98%. I would report recall (missing a sick patient is costly), precision and F1 for the disease class, with the mean and spread across folds, and compare them with the baseline and a simple model.
model_answer.zh: I would split by patient so that scans of one patient never appear in both training and test data (otherwise the model can recognise the patient and the estimate is optimistic). With 500 patients and about 10 positives, I would use stratified k-fold cross-validation (k = 5), keeping the 2% positive rate in each fold, tuning hyperparameters inside the training folds and keeping a final test set untouched until the end. I would not use accuracy, since the Zero-R baseline already has 98%. I would report recall (missing a sick patient is costly), precision and F1 for the disease class, with the mean and spread across folds, and compare them with the baseline and a simple model.

explain.en: A design answer states the split, the metric and the baseline, each with its reason.
explain.zh: 设计题要写出划分、指标和基线，每一项都带理由。

title.zh: 要记住的

rows.en: performance on unseen data; train / validation (tune) / test (once); leakage = test information reaching training or model choice
rows.zh: 在没见过的数据上的表现；训练/验证（调参）/测试（一次）；泄漏 = 测试信息进入训练或选模型

rows.en: simple, reproducible; split size and sampling bias; wastes data
rows.zh: 简单、可复现；划分大小与抽样偏差；浪费数据

rows.en: keeps class proportions; use for imbalance
rows.zh: 保持类别比例；用于不平衡数据

rows.en: mean of k scores; every instance tested once; k = 10 usual; LOO k = N, slowest
rows.zh: k 个分数的平均；每个实例测试一次；常用 k = 10；留一 k = N，最慢

rows.en: $(TP+TN)/N$; $1-$ accuracy; compare with the Zero-R / One-R baseline
rows.zh: $(TP+TN)/N$；$1-$ 准确率；要和 Zero-R / One-R 基线比

rows.en: $TP/(TP+FP)$ column; $TP/(TP+FN)$ row; the threshold trades one for the other
average over classes; every class equal; emphasises small classes
rows.zh: 按类平均；每类等权；强调小类

rows.en: pool the counts; every instance equal; dominated by large classes; micro-P = micro-R = micro-F1 = accuracy (single label)
rows.zh: 汇总计数；每个实例等权；被大类主导；单标签时 micro-P = micro-R = micro-F1 = 准确率
